author: haiku
label: c2-nat-haiku-01
changes: Added a terms section, defining token, hash, active, revoke, bearer header, CSPRNG, row lock, primary, flush and GREATEST.
Moved the decisions into short notes after the diagram, and removed the repeated copies of the same rules from the decisions and the state table.
Added the no-valid-session 401 branch to Flows 1, 2 and 4, and a matching row in the failure table.
Added id, user_id, revoked_at null and last_used_at null to the Flow 1 INSERT, and stated where each value comes from.
Added id to the Flow 2 SELECT, because revoke needs the id.
Split the Flow 4 zero-row case: a SELECT tells an already-revoked own token (204) from an unknown or another user's token (404).
Stated in the lost-response branch that the browser shows status unknown and does not retry the POST, with the reason.
Stated that tokens carry the owner's full rights, since the brief defines no scopes.
Explained in the notes why a crash loses at most one interval and why a second server instance would still keep rows correct.
Added an open-questions section for disabled or deleted users, row retention and the browser timeout.
Kept every requirement and failure row from the first version, including log redaction, read routing, route scope, CSRF, rate limit and orphan monitoring under checks before build.
Flow 3 of the diagram: added a branch for a bearer lookup error or timeout, which returns 500 with a generic body and does not run the request (Q9).

Flow 3 of the diagram: the 5-minute flush now swaps the live map for an empty one, writes the snapshot by token id with GREATEST, drops the snapshot only after commit, and merges it back on failure (Q10).
Notes, Bearer check: stated that a failed lookup is refused with 500 and never runs, so a database error cannot admit a token (Q9).
Notes, Last-used: rewritten to describe the swap, the snapshot, the per-id UPDATE with GREATEST, and the merge-back on failure, in place of the earlier single sentence (Q10).
Where state lives, Last used row: added the snapshot held during a flush (Q10).
What happens when things fail: added a row for a bearer lookup error or timeout (Q9), and changed the last-used flush failure row to say the snapshot is merged back into memory (Q10).
Kept every requirement from the brief and every other part of the first version unchanged.
Rewrote the whole document once for a newcomer, in the skill's order: what this is, terms, diagram, notes, state, failures, rollout checks, open questions.
Merged the first version's 'Decisions before the diagram' section into the summary, the terms and the notes, so each fact appears once. The Where state and Failure tables are kept, with the new rows.

Added terms for session, hash, active, revoke, bearer header, CSPRNG, unique index, row lock, primary, last used, flush, snapshot, GREATEST and CSRF, since a newcomer to this stack would not know them.
Added the session check as an explicit first step of every settings call, with 401 rather than a redirect and a failure row (junior Q1).
Stated in Create where id, user_id, revoked_at and last_used_at come from, and that expires_at is created_at plus 90 days (Q2).
Stated that the last-used map lives in the one server process, and what would change with more instances (Q3).
Stated the 1-hour allowance source in the List and Last-used notes (Q4).
Wrote out the revoke zero-row logic: one SELECT, 204 for this user's already-revoked token, 404 for unknown or other users' tokens, with the reason (Q5).
Explained why the browser does not retry the POST and how it detects status unknown, and kept the open timeout question (Q6).
Stated the same-rights-as-user rule in Bearer call, with the disabled or deleted user question kept open (Q7).
Stated that expired and revoked rows are never deleted and how they leave the limit and the list (Q8).
Added the bearer lookup error or timeout branch, the 500 response, the reason it is not a 401, and its failure table row (Q9).
Expanded the flush into four numbered steps: swap the map, batched GREATEST UPDATE by token id, drop the snapshot on success, merge back on failure (Q10).
Moved rollout checks into their own section, separate from how the system runs, and marked CSRF as needing confirmation.
Removed repeated statements, such as the lost-response reasoning and the limit, so each is said in one place. No requirement, limit, number or failure row from the brief or first version was dropped.
